title: AWM-Fuse: Multi-Modality Image Fusion for Adverse Weather via Global and Local Text Perception

contributions.improvement: Effectively handle multiple degradations simultaneously in adverse weather conditions.
contributions.implementation_detail: Leverages global and local text perception within a unified, shared-weight architecture.
Proposed novel global and local text perception modules that guide feature extraction from both macro and micro perspectives.
contributions.improve_from: Existing studies with limited textual embedding design and overemphasis on local details.

contributions.improvement: Improved fusion image restoration and better alignment with real semantic labels.
contributions.implementation_detail: Proposed a novel VLM-driven loss using CLIP to guide fusion image restoration, introducing rich and high-quality textual descriptions for multi-modality images under adverse weather.
contributions.improve_from: Prior VLM-guided methods (limited to image restoration/enhancement, lacking generalization to IVIF, and clean semantic text descriptions).

contributions.improvement: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in complex weather conditions and downstream tasks.
contributions.implementation_detail: Extensive experiments under diverse adverse weather conditions.

limitations: Extracting features using the VLM model inevitably incurs additional computational overhead, leading to higher FLOPs and parameters compared to some methods.

datasets.details: Contains both real and synthetic samples for three adverse weather types: rain, haze, and snow. Used for adverse weather evaluation.

experiment_setup.training_details: 700 images for each type of adverse weather (rain, haze, and snow) from the AWMM-100k dataset were combined into a single dataset of 2100 image pairs. Each image was randomly cropped to 160x160 pixels, with a batch size of 2. The Adam optimizer was used with an initial learning rate of 1x10^-3, and the model was trained for over 300 epochs. RSSBs employ a U-Net structure, with the block configuration of each layer set to [8, 10, 10, 12, 10, 10, 8]. Feature channels in the RSSBs progressively increase from 48 to 384 and are then reduced back to 48 channels.
